templates.name: Windows by Netwatch WMI
templates.description:
Netwatch - Windows OS monitoring (agentless WMI): CPU, memory, disk, network, services, plus domain name and role.
Provider: Netwatch.
Link to every Windows host. Domain controllers additionally get "Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI".

items.name: Domain name
items.description: DNS name of the domain this DC belongs to.

items.name: Domain role
items.description: Win32_ComputerSystem.DomainRole. 4 = backup DC, 5 = primary DC (holds the PDC emulator role).

triggers.name: AD DS: Domain role has changed
triggers.event_name: AD DS: Domain role has changed (now: {ITEM.VALUE})
triggers.description: DomainRole changed. Usually the PDC emulator FSMO role was moved to or from this DC. Acknowledge to close.

items.name: Context switches per second
items.description: The combined rate at which all processors are switched from one thread to another.

items.name: CPU DPC time
items.description: The time a processor spent receiving and servicing deferred procedure calls (DPCs). Sustained high values may indicate a processor bottleneck or a driver/hardware issue.

items.name: CPU interrupt time
items.description: The percent of time the processor spends handling hardware interrupts. A value above 20% suggests possible hardware issues.

triggers.name: Windows: CPU interrupt time is too high
triggers.event_name: Windows: CPU interrupt time is too high (over {$CPU.INTERRUPT.CRIT.MAX}% for 5m)
triggers.description: The CPU Interrupt Time in the last 5 minutes exceeds {$CPU.INTERRUPT.CRIT.MAX}%.

items.name: CPU privileged time
items.description: The percent of time that the processor spent executing in Kernel (Privileged) mode.

triggers.name: Windows: CPU privileged time is too high
triggers.event_name: Windows: CPU privileged time is too high (over {$CPU.PRIV.CRIT.MAX}% for 5m)
triggers.description: The CPU privileged time in the last 5 minutes exceeds {$CPU.PRIV.CRIT.MAX}%.

dependencies.name: Windows: CPU interrupt time is too high

items.name: CPU queue length
items.description: The number of threads observed as delayed in the processor ready queue, waiting to be executed.

items.name: CPU user time
items.description: The percent of time that the processor(s) spent executing in User mode.

items.name: ICMP ping
items.description: Host reachability by ICMP. Requires fping on the Zabbix server/proxy.

triggers.name: Unavailable by ICMP ping
triggers.description: Last three ICMP checks failed. The host is down or unreachable from Zabbix.

items.name: ICMP loss
items.description: ICMP packet loss.

triggers.expression: min(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/icmppingloss,5m)>{$AD.ICMP.LOSS.WARN} and min(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/icmppingloss,5m)<100
triggers.name: High ICMP ping loss
triggers.description: ICMP packet loss is above {$AD.ICMP.LOSS.WARN}% for 5m.

items.name: ICMP response time
items.description: ICMP round-trip time.

triggers.name: High ICMP ping response time
triggers.description: Average ICMP response time is above {$AD.ICMP.RESPONSE.WARN}s for 5m.

items.name: Cache bytes
items.description: Cache Bytes is the sum of the Memory\System Cache Resident Bytes, Memory\System Driver Resident Bytes, Memory\System Code Resident Bytes, and Memory\Pool Paged Resident Bytes counters. This counter displays the last observed value only; it is not an average.

items.name: Free system page table entries
items.description: The number of page table entries not currently in use by the system. If the number is less than 5,000, there may be a memory leak or the system may be running out of memory.

triggers.name: Windows: Number of free system page table entries is too low
triggers.event_name: Windows: Number of free system page table entries is too low (less {$MEM.PAGE_TABLE_CRIT.MIN} for 5m)
triggers.description: Free System Page Table Entries has been less than {$MEM.PAGE_TABLE_CRIT.MIN} for 5 minutes. There may be a memory leak.

items.name: Memory page faults per second
items.description: The average number of pages faulted per second, including both hard and soft faults.

items.name: Memory pages per second
items.description: The rate at which pages are read from or written to disk to resolve hard page faults. If greater than 1,000, there may be a memory leak.

triggers.name: Windows: The Memory Pages/sec is too high
triggers.event_name: Windows: The Memory Pages/sec is too high (over {$MEM.PAGE_SEC.CRIT.MAX} for 5m)
triggers.description: Memory Pages/sec in the last 5 minutes exceeds {$MEM.PAGE_SEC.CRIT.MAX}. There may be a memory leak.

items.name: Memory pool non-paged
items.description: The size, in bytes, of the non-paged pool. A possible memory leak is indicated if the value is greater than 175MB (100MB with the /3GB switch).

items.name: Number of processes
items.description: The number of processes.

items.name: Free swap space in %
items.description: The free space of the swap volume/file expressed in %.

items.name: Used swap space in %
items.description: The used space of the swap volume/file in percent.

items.name: CPU utilization
items.description: CPU utilization expressed in %.

triggers.name: Windows: High CPU utilization
triggers.description: CPU utilization is too high. The system might be slow to respond.

triggers.name: Windows: WMI polling is not available
triggers.event_name: Windows: WMI polling is not available (or nodata for {$WMI.NODATA_TIMEOUT})
triggers.description: No data has been received from the zbxwmi checks for {$WMI.NODATA_TIMEOUT}. This usually means the host is unreachable, WMI/DCOM access is blocked, or the credentials in {$WMI.USER}/{$WMI.PASSWORD} are wrong.

triggers.expression: change(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/system.hostname) and length(last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/system.hostname))>0
triggers.name: Windows: System name has changed
triggers.event_name: Windows: System name has changed (new name: {ITEM.VALUE})
triggers.description: The name of the system has changed. Acknowledge to close the problem manually.

items.name: System local time
items.description: The local system time of the host, converted from the WMI CIM_DATETIME format.

items.name: Free swap space
items.description: The free space of the swap volume/file expressed in bytes.

items.name: Total swap space
items.description: The total space of the swap volume/file expressed in bytes.

items.name: Number of threads
items.description: The number of threads used by all running processes.

items.name: Uptime
items.description: System uptime, computed from Win32_OperatingSystem.LastBootUpTime.

triggers.name: Windows: Host has been restarted
triggers.description: The device uptime is less than 10 minutes.

items.name: Total memory
items.description: Total physical memory expressed in bytes.

items.name: Used memory
items.description: Used physical memory expressed in bytes (Total - Free).

items.name: Memory utilization
items.description: Memory utilization in %.

triggers.name: Windows: High memory utilization
triggers.description: The system is running out of free memory.

items.name: Number of cores
items.description: The number of logical processors available on the computer.

items.name: Page file usage WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_PageFileUsage data.

items.name: Memory counters WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_Memory counters, used as the master item for several dependent items.

items.name: System info WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_OperatingSystem data, used as the master item for several dependent items.

items.name: System counters WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System counters.

items.name: Computer system WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_ComputerSystem Domain and DomainRole.

items.name: Windows: Network interfaces WMI get
items.description: Raw data of Win32_NetworkAdapter.

items.name: CPU counters WMI get
items.description: Raw aggregate (_Total) Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_Processor counters.

items.name: Paging file WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_PagingFile counter for the combined paging files.

items.name: AD member servers get
items.description: Computer objects from AD plus their IP from the DC DNS server (zbxwmi-auth -members).

discovery_rules.name: Network interfaces discovery
discovery_rules.description: Discovery of installed network interfaces via WMI (Win32_NetworkAdapter).

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Inbound packets discarded
item_prototypes.description: The number of incoming packets dropped on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Inbound packets with errors
item_prototypes.description: The number of incoming packets with errors on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Bits received
item_prototypes.description: Incoming traffic on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Outbound packets discarded
item_prototypes.description: The number of outgoing packets dropped on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Outbound packets with errors
item_prototypes.description: The number of outgoing packets with errors on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Bits sent
item_prototypes.description: Outgoing traffic on the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Speed
item_prototypes.description: Estimated bandwidth of the network interface, if any.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Operational status
item_prototypes.description: The operational status of the network interface.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"])<>2 and (last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#1)<>last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#2))
trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
trigger_prototypes.description: This trigger fires if the operational status is down and can be disabled per interface via {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Interface type
item_prototypes.description: The type of the network interface.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Counters WMI get
item_prototypes.description: Raw Win32_PerfFormattedData_Tcpip_NetworkInterface counters for this adapter. Note: the instance Name in this class can differ from the adapter name reported by Win32_NetworkAdapter (special characters are replaced with "_") — verify manually if this item returns no data.

trigger_prototypes.expression:
change(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"])<0 and
last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"])>0 and
last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"])=2
trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Ethernet has changed to lower speed than it was before
trigger_prototypes.description: This Ethernet connection has transitioned down from its known maximum speed. This might be a sign of autonegotiation issues. Acknowledge to close the problem manually.

dependencies.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"])<>2 and (last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#1)<>last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression:
(avg(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.in["{#IFGUID}"],15m)>({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}/100)*last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"]) or
avg(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.out["{#IFGUID}"],15m)>({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}/100)*last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"])) and
last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"])>0
trigger_prototypes.recovery_expression:
avg(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.in["{#IFGUID}"],15m)<(({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}-3)/100)*last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"]) and
avg(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.out["{#IFGUID}"],15m)<(({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}-3)/100)*last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.speed["{#IFGUID}"])
trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High bandwidth usage
trigger_prototypes.description: The utilization of the network interface is close to its estimated maximum bandwidth.

dependencies.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"])<>2 and (last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#1)<>last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression:
min(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.in["{#IFGUID}",errors],5m)>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}
or min(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.out["{#IFGUID}",errors],5m)>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}
trigger_prototypes.recovery_expression:
max(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.in["{#IFGUID}",errors],5m)<{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}*0.8
and max(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.out["{#IFGUID}",errors],5m)<{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}*0.8
trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High error rate
trigger_prototypes.event_name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High error rate (>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"} for 5m)
trigger_prototypes.description: It recovers when it is below 80% of the {$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"} threshold.

dependencies.name: Windows: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"])<>2 and (last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#1)<>last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/net.if.status["{#IFGUID}"],#2))

discovery_rules.name: Filesystem discovery
discovery_rules.description: Discovery of local fixed disk drives (filesystems) via WMI (Win32_LogicalDisk).

item_prototypes.name: FS [{#WMI.VOLUMENAME}({#WMI.DEVICEID})]: Space: Used, in %
item_prototypes.description: Calculated as the percentage of currently used space compared to the total available space.

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: FS [{#WMI.VOLUMENAME}({#WMI.DEVICEID})]: Space is critically low
trigger_prototypes.event_name: Windows: FS [{#WMI.VOLUMENAME}({#WMI.DEVICEID})]: Space is critically low (used > {$VFS.FS.PUSED.MAX.CRIT:"{#WMI.DEVICEID}"}%)
trigger_prototypes.description: The volume's space usage exceeds the {$VFS.FS.PUSED.MAX.CRIT:"{#WMI.DEVICEID}"}% limit.

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: FS [{#WMI.VOLUMENAME}({#WMI.DEVICEID})]: Space is low
trigger_prototypes.description: The volume's space usage exceeds the {$VFS.FS.PUSED.MAX.WARN:"{#WMI.DEVICEID}"}% limit.

dependencies.name: Windows: FS [{#WMI.VOLUMENAME}({#WMI.DEVICEID})]: Space is critically low

discovery_rules.name: Windows services discovery
discovery_rules.description: Discovery of Windows services via WMI (Win32_Service), filtered using the template macros.

item_prototypes.name: State of service "{#WMI.NAME}" ({#WMI.DISPLAYNAME})
item_prototypes.description: Current state as reported by Win32_Service.State (Running, Stopped, Paused, ...).

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: "{#WMI.NAME}" ({#WMI.DISPLAYNAME}) is not running
trigger_prototypes.description: The service has had a state other than "Running" for the last three polls.

discovery_rules.name: Physical disks discovery
discovery_rules.description: Discovery of physical disks via WMI (Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfDisk_PhysicalDisk).

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk utilization by idle time
item_prototypes.description: The percentage of elapsed time that the disk was busy servicing read or write requests, derived from idle time.

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk is overloaded
trigger_prototypes.description: The disk appears to be under heavy load.

dependencies.name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk read request responses are too high
Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk write request responses are too high

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk average queue size (avgqu-sz)
item_prototypes.description: The current average disk queue: the number of requests outstanding while performance data is being collected.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk read request avg waiting time
item_prototypes.description: The average time for read requests to be served, including time spent in queue.

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk read request responses are too high
trigger_prototypes.event_name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk read request responses are too high (read > {$VFS.DEV.READ.AWAIT.WARN:"{#WMI.NAME}"}s for 15m)
trigger_prototypes.description: This trigger might indicate the disk {#WMI.NAME} is saturated.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Average disk read queue length
item_prototypes.description: The number of read requests outstanding on the disk at the time the performance data is collected.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk read rate
item_prototypes.description: Rate of read operations on the disk.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk write request avg waiting time
item_prototypes.description: The average time for write requests to be served, including time spent in queue.

trigger_prototypes.name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk write request responses are too high
trigger_prototypes.event_name: Windows: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk write request responses are too high (write > {$VFS.DEV.WRITE.AWAIT.WARN:"{#WMI.NAME}"}s for 15m)
trigger_prototypes.description: This trigger might indicate the disk {#WMI.NAME} is saturated.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Average disk write queue length
item_prototypes.description: The number of write requests outstanding on the disk at the time the performance data is collected.

item_prototypes.name: {#WMI.NAME}: Disk write rate
item_prototypes.description: Rate of write operations on the disk.

discovery_rules.name: Domain member servers discovery
discovery_rules.description: Reads enabled, non-DC computer accounts from AD and creates a host for each member server, linked to this same template and reached by the IP found in the DC's DNS. They inherit the WMI credential macros from the DC host. Runs only where {$AD.MEMBER.DISCOVERY}=1 (the DC).

macros.description: Discovered member servers must not run member discovery themselves.

1 = create hosts for domain member servers found in AD. Set to 0 automatically on the hosts it creates.

Regex of computer names NOT to create as hosts.

The threshold of the % Privileged Time counter.

Disk read average response time (in s) before the trigger fires.

triggers.expression: min(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/cpu.queue_length,5m) - last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/zbxwmi-auth["{$WMI.USER}","{$WMI.PASSWORD}","{$WMI.DOMAIN}","-action","get","-fields","NumberOfLogicalProcessors","Win32_ComputerSystem",{HOST.CONN}]) * 2 > {$CPU.QUEUE.CRIT.MAX}
triggers.name: Windows: CPU queue length is too high
triggers.event_name: Windows: CPU queue length is too high (over {$CPU.QUEUE.CRIT.MAX} for 5m)
triggers.description: The CPU Queue Length in the last 5 minutes exceeds {$CPU.QUEUE.CRIT.MAX}. Processor Queue Length should not exceed the number of cores * 2 for long. Tune via {$CPU.QUEUE.CRIT.MAX}.

triggers.expression: max(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/swap.pfree,5m)<{$SWAP.PFREE.MIN.WARN} and last(/Windows by Netwatch WMI/system.swap.size[,total])>0
triggers.name: Windows: High swap space usage
triggers.event_name: Windows: High swap space usage (less than {$SWAP.PFREE.MIN.WARN}% free)
triggers.description: This trigger is ignored if there is no swap configured.
